objectives.text: Deter and, if deterrence fails, hold the line against Russia on a frontier that is only a few hundred kilometres wide: the Suwalki corridor between Kaliningrad and Belarus. The state's own intelligence says Russia could be ready for a limited conflict in the Baltic region within 3-5 years of a ceasefire in Ukraine (1-2 years if sanctions are lifted), so the aim is to be a costlier target than the neighbours.

objectives.text: Keep the allies physically on the ground and bind them with money: a permanent German brigade (full by 2027), a rotational US presence that Vilnius now offers to pay for as a permanent base, NATO's forward land forces, and a national division by 2030 financed by EU loans. Defence spending is the currency - 5.38% of GDP in 2026 and at least about 5% planned for 2027.

Dependence now runs west and north, to Poland, Germany, the Nordics and the EU budget.

constraints.text: Geography: the Suwalki corridor between Kaliningrad and Belarus carries the only land link to the rest of NATO, and Russia's GPS spoofing from Kaliningrad has grown from 3 to 36 antennas in a year. Whatever Lithuania builds, it cannot choose where the front is.

paradoxes.text: The more Lithuania secures itself by treaty exit and fortification, the more it gives Moscow and Minsk to point at. Leaving the cluster-munitions and Ottawa conventions and moving to lift the constitutional ban on nuclear weapons buy capability and a seat in NATO's deterrent, but each step is cited in Moscow as proof of aggression (Russia criticised the nuclear amendment and the proposed US base in the same week) and costs the moral standing Lithuania uses to lead on Ukraine and sanctions.

paradoxes.text: Closing the Belarus border protects Lithuania and hurts Lithuanians. Shutting the last two crossings (27 Oct-20 Nov 2025) answered the balloons, but Minsk answered by detaining Lithuanian trucks (about 280 to over 1,000, up to 200 still held in May 2026) and a decree banning Lithuanian-plated trucks to the end of 2027; the same sanctions policy has cost Klaipeda a third of its peak turnover and drawn a EUR 12bn arbitration claim, while Washington presses Vilnius to reopen the potash route.

paradoxes.text: Lithuania keeps Russian gas flowing to Kaliningrad so as not to hand Moscow a pretext on the corridor it fears most. It renewed the Amber Grid-Gazprom transit to 2030 (about EUR 30m of allowed revenue in 2026) while calling Russia the main threat: the border it must defend is also a commercial artery it must keep open, and closing it was floated and withdrawn in the Oct 2025 balloon crisis.

Vilnius volunteered the money on 29 Sep-6 Oct 2026, three days before Trump's diesel deal weakened the sanctions front Lithuania leads and months after the US pressed for the Belarus potash route; the more Lithuania pays for US attention, the more it needs the policy that attention is supposed to protect.

The president and foreign minister hold a hard line on China and Taiwan (only Taipei may rename its office), while the government programme seeks normalisation and a coalition partner wants the office renamed within two months; every signal to Beijing is read in Washington, where the former defence minister warned it could look like a move against US interests. A normalisation that fails would leave Lithuania with neither China's market nor a clear position with Taiwan.

grand_strategy.reading:
Lithuania is a small state that has chosen to be a front-line state on purpose:
it argues for the threat louder than anyone and buys the insurance before the
allies are asked to. The ranked objectives are a ladder from Russia, to the
allies' soldiers, to Ukraine, and the means mirror them - the most defence
spending in NATO relative to GDP, borrowed money from the EU to turn a brigade
into a division, and treaty exits that trade moral position for capability.
The Luttwakian friction appears wherever one rung undermines another. Border
closure and sanctions on Belarus defend the frontier but hand Minsk hostages;
leaving the mine and cluster conventions and lifting the nuclear ban deter
Moscow but enlarge Moscow's narrative; and the offer to pay for a permanent
US base binds the security of the state to a patron that is simultaneously
easing sanctions on Russian diesel and Belarusian potash. Domestic politics
adds noise, not direction: three Social Democratic cabinets in two years, a
president and a foreign minister who anchor the line on Russia, Ukraine and
Poland, and an open split on China. The Russia grade is adversary because the
Seimas calls its regime terrorist and the national assessments treat it as the
only state that can attack Lithuania; Belarus is a rival because Vilnius
aims at pressure and isolation, not at the end of the regime, and the line
softens when Washington pushes. The year to watch is 2027: the German brigade
complete, the nuclear amendment's final vote (planned 12 Jan 2027), the EU
sanctions renewal on potash, and a US rotation that may or may not become a base.

stances.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded from adversary to rival for consistency with Estonia, Latvia-to-be and Poland; 'adversary' is reserved for actors seeking each other's destruction (Iran-Israel), while Lithuania seeks deterrence and a Russian defeat in Ukraine, not the end of the Russian state. The Seimas 'terrorist state' resolutions are the hardest rhetoric in NATO but the structural position is the same as its Baltic neighbours'. Reserved for mortal enemies, and the evidence is a declared view of Russia's regime, not rhetoric: the Seimas voted in May 2022 that Russia supports and perpetrates terrorism, and in March 2023 asked the world to recognise it as a terrorist state; the 2026 national threat assessment treats Russia as the primary threat and dates a limited Baltic war to 3-5 years after a Ukraine ceasefire. Hostile action is documented on Lithuanian soil (IKEA arson sentenced Nov 2025, 36 GPS-spoofing antennas in Kaliningrad). Lithuania does not seek Russia's disappearance, which is why this is the edge of the grade; the Russian regime's behaviour is the problem, and it backs Ukraine's victory by law (0.25% of GDP). Cooling: 'cooling' here means hardening. Residual commerce (Kaliningrad gas transit to 2030) is a legal obligation, not a bond. Bond - grievance: the 1940-91 occupation. The reciprocal Russian stance has not been written.

stances.note: Mirror of Belarus's own stance toward Lithuania, with the same evidence. Lithuania hosted Tsikhanouskaya's office from 2020 (it moved to Warsaw in Feb 2026), banned Belarusian potash transit via Klaipeda in 2022 and refuses to reopen it while EU sanctions stand (Budrys, Dec 2025 and May 2026), closed its last two crossings on 27 Oct-20 Nov 2025 over the balloons, blocks Astravets power, and the Sinkevicius programme (Jul 2026) keeps isolating Minsk. Rival and not adversary: the aim is pressure and isolation, not the end of the regime, Vilnius is divided on easing (47/46 in an LRT poll cited by Belarus's card), and Washington is pressing for transit and a deputy-minister contact. Trend stable: Lithuania holds while the US softens. No source uses the word 'rival': our reading (confidence C). Bond - grievance: sanctions, the exile base and the seized trucks. Belarus's own card grades Lithuania rival too, so the pair is symmetric.

stances.note: Mirror of Poland's own stance toward Lithuania, with the same exercise and visit sources, plus what the Lithuanian side adds. The Suwalki gap is the shared hinge: Gallant Boar 2026, Brave Griffin 26-II observed by Nausėda and Nawrocki in May 2026, a second Vilnius-Augustow dual-use route, a cross-border civilian evacuation plan (Sep 2026), the Via Baltica section opened by both presidents in Oct 2025. NATO and EU co-members; Poland-Lithuania friction (names in Polish diacritics, minority schools; the Orlen/Mazeikiai refinery history) is recurring but not structural. Bond - affinity: the shared Commonwealth past.

Lithuania bought 44 Leopard 2A8 through Germany's procurement office (EUR 950m). The Sinkevicius programme lists completing the deployment by 2027. Co-member of NATO and EU; no friction found. stances.note: Co-member of NATO with a visible friction, so the ontology's rule applies: reluctant_ally, not ally. Vilnius wants more American presence than Washington offers: the armoured battalion of about 1,000 left in June 2026 with the next rotation 'under review' (first gap since 2020), a new rotation of up to 1,000 is due in late October, and on 6 Oct 2026 the PM offered to pay for a permanent base while Trump said 'we will certainly look at it'. Against that: US sanctions on Belarusian potash lifted in March 2026 and Washington pressing Lithuania to reopen transit, and Trump's diesel deal with Putin (9 Oct 2026), which Lithuania said weakens the Western position. Lithuania does not hedge: no alternative patron, hence stable and not cooling. No source uses the exact word 'reluctant': our reading (confidence C). Bond - affinity: non-recognition of the 1940 annexation and the pro-American public.

Government instability (Paluckas, Ruginiene, Sinkevicius) has not touched the line; a Lithuanian, Kubilius, is the defence commissioner. stances.note: Baltic neighbour, NATO and EU co-member, and Lithuania's largest export market (12.4% of exports, Jan-Aug 2025). The three Baltic ministries approved the Baltic Defence Line concept on 19 Jan 2024; Latvia is slower than Estonia on bunkers and has kept its Belarus crossings shut since Sep 2023, while Lithuania reopened after one month in 2025. Latvia and Estonia objected to Lithuania's push for an earlier desynchronisation date (Litgrid's agreement settled on Feb 2025). The Oct 2026 armed incident on the Latvian border with Belarus is a shared frontline issue. Bond - affinity: the Baltic common fate.

stances.note: Beijing downgraded relations to chargé d'affaires and imposed informal trade restrictions after the Taiwanese Representative Office opened in Vilnius in Nov 2021 (customs delisting, credit lines closed, rail freight suspended). stances_toward.note: Lithuania is Belarus's sharpest neighbour: it hosted Tsikhanouskaya's office since 2020, closed Klaipeda to Belarusian potash, is the veto-holder on the EU potash question (Budrys, 26 May 2026) and was the target of the smuggling balloons that shut Vilnius airport (Oct 2025, Jan and Apr 2026). It closed its last two crossings on 27-29 Oct 2025 until 20 Nov, and Minsk answered by holding Lithuanian trucks (about 200 still detained in May 2026) and by a EUR 12bn arbitration claim. Cooling, not adversary: the crossings reopened, Washington is pressing for better Belarus-Lithuania ties (Coale, Mar 2026) and Vilnius is divided on easing (47/46 in an LRT poll). No source uses the word 'rival': our reading (confidence C). Bond - grievance: sanctions on potash and the exile base.

relations_from.summary: Agreement signed in Vilnius on 18 Dec 2023 on the permanent stationing of the 45th Panzer Brigade (about 4,800 soldiers and 200 civilians at Rudninkai and Rukla); an intergovernmental agreement of Sep 2024 set the legal basis. Formally established 1 Apr 2025, full operational capability promised for end-2027; in Sep 2026 the Bundeswehr moved to compulsory postings because volunteers fell short.
relations_from.note: Press figures differ on how many posts were unfilled (about 2,000 of 4,800; 'about 60% filled by volunteers'). The compulsory-posting decision is reported via Bild and has no official ministry text in our sources.
